ops.body:
Second negative result 2026-07-25 — investigation paused, still NOT root-caused. Recording so the next attempt starts past this.

Built a second repro (/tmp/lockrepro/repro2.py) faithful to the pytest harness in the ways the first one was not: it mirrors `_codex_ask` by building the binary into a temp PLUGIN_ROOT layout (`bin/../AGENTS.md`) rather than using a loose build, and mirrors `_codex_env` exactly — stub codex first on PATH, `TMPDIR` and `CODEX_ASK_RUNS_DIR` both pinned to the same per-run temp dir, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` popped. Same sequence as the golden: blocking stub, wait for `pid`, launch the same-lane replacement, poll after 0.5s, capture stderr on escape.

Result: **0/25**. Combined with the first harness's 0/15, that is 40 standalone attempts with zero reproductions, against a test that flakes reliably under pytest (1/5 isolated at a clean HEAD worktree, 1/12 isolated after the lock-protocol pass landed).

So the trigger is something about executing inside the pytest process tree — its environment, its signal/scheduling profile, or concurrent load — and not plain lock contention, which is what both harnesses actually exercise. The EINTR-on-Flock hypothesis is therefore still unconfirmed; do not add a retry loop to `acquireLaneLock` on the strength of it.

Also confirmed: the lock-protocol pass (classify read-only, non-blocking prune lock, watch shared lock, readPid > 0, XDG canonicalization) did NOT fix this. Measured 1 failure in 12 isolated runs afterwards. It also did not measurably worsen it, though the samples are too small to claim either direction.

Still the cheapest next step, and still unexecuted: capture the replacement's stderr from a genuinely failing pytest run. The test asserts at test_scaffold.py:1398 before `communicate()`, so the message is discarded. A conftest-level or temporary in-test capture would discriminate `cannot open lane lock` (registry.go:89) from `cannot acquire lane lock` (registry.go:97) in one shot and either confirm or kill EINTR immediately. Everything upstream of that is now ruled out by elimination — see the previous comment.
